# /launch medium — weekly briefing newsletter signup page

Intent: a signup page for the weekly briefing newsletter targeted at SMB operators who manage multiple SaaS tools.

## Mock gallery (3 variants)

### Variant A — Tufte (data over decoration)
Headline: "47 tools your team uses. One briefing. 20 minutes a week."
Proof: sparkline of open rates for last 12 weeks across 1,200 subscribers.
Typography: Charter at 18px body, 36px headline. One typeface family.
Color palette: ink on cream. Two accents (red for high weeks, green for recent uptick).
Hero image: none. Density first.
URL: /tmp/launch-tufte/
Spec snippet: 2-column grid, data-table for recent issues, signup form sidebar.

### Variant B — Rams (less, but better)
Headline: "The weekly briefing for people who build small things."
Proof: one testimonial, one byline, white space.
Typography: Helvetica Neue. 42px headline. 20px body.
Color palette: neutral grays plus one brand color for the CTA.
Hero image: large grayscale photo.
URL: /tmp/launch-rams/
Spec snippet: single-column centered layout, 60% viewport max-width.

### Variant C — Walker (editorial voice)
Headline: "You read 40 tabs this week. This one is on us."
Proof: three recent topic tags with hover-preview cards.
Typography: Walker Studios typeface at 48px headline, Reader at 17px body.
Color palette: full-bleed background, dynamic per-issue.
Hero image: generated collage from this week's coverage.
URL: /tmp/launch-walker/
Spec snippet: full-width hero, scroll-triggered reveal, inline tag preview cards.

## Buildable spec

System: a Next.js signup form POST-ing to a Postgres table. Rate-limited at 3 sign-ups per minute per IP. Email validation via Zod schema at API boundary. Confirmation email sent via Resend SDK with signed unsubscribe token (HS256, 30-day expiry). Signup events logged to Posthog with UTM capture.

## INVEST user stories (5)

1. As a reader, I can see the headline in under 2 seconds so I know what the briefing covers.
2. As a reader, I can sign up with just an email so I don't abandon the form.
3. As the operator, I can see weekly sign-up counts in Posthog so I know if the hero is working.
4. As a reader, I can confirm my subscription from the welcome email so my address is verified.
5. As the operator, I can see per-variant conversion data so I can pick the winning hero.

Next: pick a variant. Then say "/build <variant>" to ship it.
